author.name: Yifan Dai, Zhenhua Wu, Bohan Zeng, Daili Hua, Jialing Liu, Bozhou Li, Yuran Wang, Chengzhuo Tong, Hao Liang, Xiaochen Ma, Junbo Niu, Tianyu Guo, Yang Shi, Yue Ding, Yiyan Ji, Bingyin Mei, Yushuo Guan, Yuanxing Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Fangcheng Fu, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes LatentOmni, a cross-modal reasoning framework that interleaves textual reasoning with audio-visual latent representations, arguing that unified latent space preserves dense sensory information better than text-based chain-of-thought.

entry.title: Understanding Data Temporality Impact on Large Language Models Pre-training

author.name: Pilchen Hippolyte, Fabre Romain, Signe Talla Franck, Perez Patrick, Grave Edouard

entry.summary: Studies how temporal ordering of pre-training data affects factual knowledge acquisition in LLMs. Introduces a 7,000-question temporal benchmark and trains 6B-parameter models on chronologically ordered vs. shuffled Common Crawl data.

entry.title: From Parameters to Data: A Task-Parameter-Guided Fine-Tuning Pipeline for Efficient LLM Alignment

author.name: Hao Chen, Qi Zhang, Liyao Li, Zhanming Shen, Wentao Ye, Lirong Gao, Ningtao Wang, Xing Fu, Xiaoyu Shen, Junbo Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes P2D framework based on the 'Strong Map Hypothesis' - that sparse attention heads guide both data selection and parameter pruning for LLM fine-tuning. Unifies data selection and parameter-efficient fine-tuning as coupled processes.

entry.title: Check Your LLM's Secret Dictionary! Five Lines of Code Reveal What Your LLM Learned (Including What It Shouldn't Have)

author.name: Hisashi Miyashita

entry.summary: Shows that SVD of the lm_head weight matrix reveals interpretable semantic subspaces in just 5 lines of PyTorch. Analysis of GPT-OSS-120B, Gemma-2-2B, and Qwen2.5-1.5B reveals systematic differences in training data composition.

entry.title: Structured-Sparse Attention for Entity Tracking with Subquadratic Sequence Complexity

author.name: Hangyue Zhao, Paul Caillon, Erwan Fagnou, Alexandre Allauzen

entry.summary: Proposes structured-sparse attention for entity tracking that exploits the block-diagonal structure of learned attention. Achieves subquadratic O(n^{4/3}d) evaluation while keeping within-block interactions exact.

entry.title: Visual-Advantage On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ruiqi Liu, Xiaolei Lv, Gengsheng Li, Ximo Zhu, Zhiheng Wang, Zhengbo Zhang, Junkai Chen, Zhiheng Li, Bo Li, Jun Gao, Shu Wu

entry.summary: Introduces visual advantage (VA) for on-policy distillation of VLMs - measuring token-level log-probability differences when fine-grained visual detail is present vs. absent. Uses VA to identify vision-critical tokens for targeted distillation.

entry.title: WorldKV: Efficient World Memory with World Retrieval and Compression

author.name: Jung Yi, Minjae Kim, Paul Hyunbin Cho, Wooseok Jang, Sangdoo Yun, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: Proposes WorldKV, a training-free framework for maintaining world consistency in autoregressive video diffusion models through World Retrieval (storing/retrieving evicted KV-cache chunks) and World Compression, enabling persistent worlds without breaking real-time constraints.

entry.title: The Attribution Impossibility: No Feature Ranking Is Faithful, Stable, and Complete Under Collinearity

author.name: Drake Caraker, Bryan Arnold, David Rhoads

entry.summary: Proves an impossibility theorem: no feature ranking can be simultaneously faithful, stable, and complete under collinearity. Resolves this via ensemble averaging (DASH) and machine-verifies with 305 Lean 4 theorems.

entry.title: Ratchet: A Minimal Hygiene Recipe for Self-Evolving LLM Agents

author.name: Xing Zhang, Yanwei Cui, Guanghui Wang, Ziyuan Li, Wei Qiu, Bing Zhu, Peiyang He

entry.summary: Introduces Ratchet, a single-agent loop where a frozen LLM writes, retrieves, curates, and retires its own skills. Addresses the finding that LLM-authored skills provide +0.0pp without lifecycle management. Achieves significant gains with Claude Opus 4.7.

entry.title: DeepWeb-Bench: A Deep Research Benchmark Demanding Massive Cross-Source Evidence and Long-Horizon Derivation

author.name: Sixiong Xie, Zhuofan Shi, Haiyang Shen, Jiuzheng Wang, Siqi Zhong, Mugeng Liu, Chongyang Pan, Peilun Jia, Baoqing Sun, Xiang Jing, Yun Ma

entry.summary: DeepWeb-Bench introduces a substantially harder benchmark for deep research systems requiring massive evidence collection, cross-source reconciliation, and long-horizon multi-step derivation, where current frontier systems struggle.

entry.title: Long-Context Reasoning Through Proxy-Based Chain-of-Thought Tuning

author.name: Miao Li, Irina Saparina, Alexander Gurung, Mirella Lapata

entry.summary: ProxyCoT transfers reasoning capabilities from short proxy contexts to full long contexts via a training framework that first learns high-quality CoT on short contexts then adapts to long inputs.

entry.title: RealUserSim: Bridging the Reality Gap in Agent Benchmarking via Grounded User Simulation

author.name: Ming Zhu, Juntao Tan, Rithesh Murthy, Jielin Qiu, Liangwei Yang, Wenting Zhao, Silvio Savarese, Shelby Heinecke, Huan Wang

entry.summary: RealUserSim grounds LLM user simulation in 14,000+ real human-LLM conversations, extracting behavioral profiles to create more realistic simulated users for agent evaluation, addressing the 'Formalism Ceiling' and 'Directive Amplification' problems.

entry.title: Spectral Unforgetting: Post-Hoc Recovery of Damaged Capabilities Without Retraining

author.name: Aarash Abro, Muhammad Tahir

entry.summary: DG-Hard is a post-hoc spectral repair method that recovers capabilities damaged by fine-tuning using only the pretrained and fine-tuned checkpoints. It treats the weight update as a low-rank task-aligned signal and separates beneficial from harmful components via spectral analysis.

entry.title: Group-Algebraic Tensors: Provably-optimal Equivariant Learning and Physical Symmetry Discovery

author.name: Paulina Hoyos, Shashanka Ubaru, Dongsung Huh, Vasileios Kalantzis, Kenneth L. Clarkson, Misha Kilmer, Haim Avron, Lior Horesh

entry.summary: Introduces the ⋆_G tensor algebra where any finite group defines the multiplication rule, making equivariance intrinsic rather than architectural. Includes machine-verified (Lean 4) proofs and Eckart-Young optimality guarantee for symmetry-preserving tensor approximation.

entry.title: Runtime-Certified Bounded-Error Quantized Attention

author.name: Dean Calver

entry.summary: Presents a tiered KV cache architecture with runtime error certification: INT8 keys and INT4 values in GPU memory with FP16 fallback in system RAM, using online error bounds to drive adaptive precision selection.

entry.title: Diagnosing Overhead in Dispatch Operations: Cross-architecture Observatory

author.name: Bole Ma, Jan Eitzinger, Harald Koestler, Gerhard Wellein

entry.summary: Introduces DODOCO, a cross-architecture observatory for diagnosing dispatch overhead in MoE expert parallelism, testing assumptions about routing imbalance across five MoE architectures including DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen3 variants.

entry.title: Grounding Driving VLA via Inverse Kinematics

author.name: Junsung Park, Hyunjung Shim

entry.summary: Reframes Driving VLA as an inverse kinematics solver, showing that trajectory prediction requires both current and future visual states as boundary conditions. Adds next visual state prediction for dense visual supervision.

entry.title: From Circuit Evidence to Mechanistic Theory: An Inductive Logic Approach

author.name: Nura Aljaafari, Danilo S. Carvalho, Andre Freitas

entry.summary: Proposes formal infrastructure for cumulative mechanistic interpretability science by treating circuit interpretation as inductive theory construction, with Causal Functional Signatures and architectural signatures learned via ILP.

entry.title: Frontier: Towards Comprehensive and Accurate LLM Inference Simulation

author.name: Yicheng Feng, Xin Tan, Yangtao Deng, Yimin Jiang, Yibo Zhu, Hong Xu

entry.summary: Presents Frontier, a discrete-event simulator for modern disaggregated LLM inference serving that captures complex parallelism, runtime optimizations, and stateful workloads like reasoning and RL rollouts.

entry.title: Mem-$\pi$: Adaptive Memory through Learning When and What to Generate

author.name: Xiaoqiang Wang, Chao Wang, Hadi Nekoei, Christopher Pal, Alexandre Lacoste, Spandana Gella, Bang Liu, Perouz Taslakian

entry.summary: Presents Mem-π, a framework for adaptive memory in LLM agents that generates context-specific guidance on demand rather than retrieving from static memory banks. Uses a separate model that jointly decides when and what guidance to produce, trained with decoupled reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Towards Understanding Self-Pretraining for Sequence Classification

author.name: Omar Coser, Loredana Zollo, Paolo Soda, Antonio Orvieto

entry.summary: Investigates why self-pretraining (masked token prediction on the same data without external data) improves Transformer sequence classification. Finds the central bottleneck is attention entropy collapse in supervised training, and SPT helps by enabling better attention distributions.

entry.title: Improved Guarantees for Constrained Online Convex Optimization via Self-Contraction

author.name: Dhruv Sarkar, Abhishek Sinha

entry.summary: Presents a projection-based algorithm for constrained online convex optimization achieving O(log T) regret and O(log T) cumulative constraint violation simultaneously for strongly convex losses, significantly improving over prior O(√(T log T)) constraint violation bounds.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Study of Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Marin Bilo\v{s}, James T. Wilson, Anderson Schneider, Yuriy Nevmyvaka

entry.summary: Mechanistic study of tabular foundation models showing they implement qualitatively distinct similarity-based readouts despite similar accuracy. Uses causal interventions to characterize how different architectures process tabular data.

entry.title: Proximal State Nudging: Reducing Skill Atrophy from AI Assistance

author.name: Megha Srivastava, Jonathan Ouyang, Eric Zhou, Andrew Silva, Emily Sumner, Dorsa Sadigh, Yuchen Cui, Deepak Gopinath, Guy Rosman

entry.summary: Proposes Proximal State Nudging for shared autonomy that balances task performance with human skill development by steering users toward learnable states, addressing skill atrophy from AI assistance.

entry.title: Distill to Think, Foresee to Act: Cognitive-Physical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yang Wu, Qiang Meng, Zhaojiang Liu, Youquan Liu, Jian Yang, Jin Xie

entry.summary: Proposes CoPhy, a cognitive-physical RL framework for autonomous driving that distills VLM knowledge into BEV encoders (discarded at inference) and uses a world model for anticipating action consequences, breaking through the imitation learning ceiling.

entry.title: Disentangling Generation and Regression in Stochastic Interpolants for Controllable Image Restoration

author.name: Yi Liu, Jia Ma, Wengen Li, Jihong Guan, Shuigeng Zhou, Yichao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes DiSI, a framework that disentangles stochastic interpolant processes into independent generation and regression components for image restoration, enabling controllable transition between high-fidelity regression and creative generation.

entry.title: Residual Skill Optimization for Text-to-SQL Ensembles

author.name: Jiongli Zhu, Haoquan Guan, Parjanya Prajakta Prashant, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Seyedeh Baharan Khatami, Canwen Xu, Xiaodong Yu, Yingyu Lin, Zhewei Yao, Yuxiong He, Babak Salimi

entry.summary: Presents DivSkill-SQL, a residual skill optimization framework for text-to-SQL ensembles where each new skill is optimized on examples the current ensemble fails on, provably targeting marginal contributions to Pass@K. Achieves +11.1 points on Spider2-Lite.

entry.title: Token-weighted Direct Preference Optimization with Attention

author.name: Chengyu Huang, Zhuohang Li, Sheng-Yen Chou, Claire Cardie

entry.summary: Proposes AttentionPO, a token-weighted DPO variant that uses the LLM's own attention to estimate token importance weights, grounded in a token-weighted RL formulation. Avoids external models or heuristic position-based weighting.

entry.title: Faithful-MR1: Faithful Multimodal Reasoning via Anchoring and Reinforcing Visual Attention

author.name: Changyuan Tian, Zhicong Lu, Huaxing Liu, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Yu Chen, Wenqian Lv, Zichuan Lin, Juncheng Diao, Deheng Ye

entry.summary: Proposes Faithful-MR1 for multimodal reasoning that anchors and reinforces visual attention during RLVR training, addressing the perception-reasoning disconnect where correctly perceived visual evidence is dropped during reasoning.

entry.title: Tokenization with Split Trees

author.name: Craig W. Schmidt, Michael Krumdick, Adam Wiemerslage, Seth Ebner, Varshini Reddy, Yuval Pinter, Chris Tanner

entry.summary: Introduces ToaST, a subword tokenization method that uses split trees and Integer Programming to directly optimize compression. The LP relaxation yields provably near-optimal vocabularies with quadratic training time scaling.

entry.title: Tokenisation via Convex Relaxations

author.name: Jan Tempus, Philip Whittington, Craig W. Schmidt, Dennis Komm, Tiago Pimentel

entry.summary: Introduces ConvexTok, a tokenization algorithm formulated as a linear program using convex optimization. Consistently improves intrinsic tokenization metrics and bits-per-byte, and provides certificates of how far a tokenizer is from optimal.

entry.title: Geometry-Adaptive Explainer for Faithful Dictionary-Based Interpretability under Distribution Shift

author.name: Sungjun Lim, Heedong Kim, Andrew Lee, Kyungwoo Song

entry.summary: Proposes Geometry-Adaptive Explainer (GAE) for maintaining dictionary-based interpretability under distribution shift. Formalizes the faithfulness gap as geometric distance between in-distribution dictionary and OOD-active subspace.

entry.title: CrossVLA: Cross-Paradigm Post-Training and Inference Optimization for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zhi Liu

entry.summary: Studies cross-paradigm VLA post-training, comparing DPO for autoregressive vs. flow-matching VLAs. Proposes surrogate log-probability estimator for applying DPO to continuous-action models and finds DoRA outperforms LoRA.

entry.title: Universal CT Representations from Anatomy to Disease Phenotype through Agglomerative Pretraining

author.name: Yuheng Li, Yuan Gao, Haoyu Dong, Yuxiang Lai, Shansong Wang, Mojtaba Safari, James E. Baciak, Xiaofeng Yang

entry.summary: Presents FlexiCT, CT foundation models trained by agglomerative continual pretraining on 266K CT volumes from 56 public datasets. Three-stage training supports slice-level, volume-level, and vision-language analysis.

entry.title: Learning Spatiotemporal Sensitivity in Video LLMs via Counterfactual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Dazhao Du, Jian Liu, Jialong Qin, Tao Han, Bohai Gu, Fangqi Zhu, Yujia Zhang, Eric Liu, Xi Chen, Song Guo

entry.summary: CRPO addresses the shortcut problem in Video LLMs during RL post-training, where models answer based on single-frame cues rather than tracking spatiotemporal dynamics. Uses counterfactual questions to enforce sensitivity to visual changes while the question remains fixed.

entry.title: Broken Memories: Detecting and Mitigating Memorization in Diffusion Models with Degraded Generations

author.name: Yuanmin Huang, Mi Zhang, Chen Chen, Feifei Li, Geng Hong, Xiaoyu You, Min Yang

entry.summary: This paper identifies that memorization in diffusion models induces internal numerical instability manifesting as visual artifacts, introduces empirical stability regions for detection, and proposes an on-the-fly framework for step-wise detection and adaptive mitigation without altering prompts.

entry.title: What Does the Caption Really Say? Counterfactual Phrase Intervention for Compositional Data Selection in Vision-Language Pretraining

author.name: Hyejin Go, Semi Lee, Hyesong Choi

entry.summary: Shows that CLIP-style pair-level filtering saturates and introduces Counterfactual Phrase Intervention (CPI), a phrase-level curation framework that measures each caption phrase's causal contribution to image-text matching. Improves compositional generalization in vision-language pretraining.

entry.title: Imagine2Real: Towards Zero-shot Humanoid-Object Interaction via Video Generative Priors

author.name: Jiahe Chen, ZiRui Wang, Feiyu Jia, Xiao Chen, Xiaojie Niu, Weishuai Zeng, Tianfan Xue, Xiaowei Zhou, Jiangmiao Pang, Jingbo Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Imagine2Real, a zero-shot framework for humanoid-object interaction that uses video generative priors and unified 4D point trajectories, tracking only sparse keypoints to bypass complex retargeting while enabling geometry-free interaction.

entry.title: TacO: Benchmarking Tactile Sensors for Object Manipulation

author.name: Anya Zorin, Zilin Si, Myungsun Park, Junsung Park, Alexiy Buynitsky, Sachin Bhadang, Taejun Park, Sohee John Yoon, Yong-Lae Park, Oliver Kroemer, Zeynep Temel, Michael T. Tolley, Sha Yi, Xiaolong Wang

entry.summary: Provides TacO, a systematic benchmark for evaluating tactile sensors across four modalities (visual, acoustic, magnetic, resistive) for robot manipulation tasks. Trains separate manipulation policies for each sensor type to provide empirical guidance on sensor selection.

entry.title: Efficient Agentic Reasoning Through Self-Regulated Simulative Planning

author.name: Mingkai Deng, Jinyu Hou, Lara S\'a Neves, Varad Pimpalkhute, Taylor W. Killian, Zhengzhong Liu, Eric P. Xing

entry.summary: Proposes a three-system architecture for agentic reasoning: simulative reasoning (world model), self-regulation (learned configurator deciding when to plan), and reactive execution. Aims for efficient token use in agent decision-making.

entry.title: Which Way Did It Move? Diagnosing and Overcoming Directional Motion Blindness in Video-LLMs

author.name: Jongseo Lee, Hyuntak Lee, Sunghun Kim, Sooa Kim, Jihoon Chung, Jinwoo Choi

entry.summary: Diagnoses 'directional motion blindness' in Video-LLMs where models perform near chance on basic directional motion questions. Localizes the failure to a direction-to-language binding problem rather than feature extraction, and proposes fixes.

entry.title: Training Language Agents to Learn from Experience

author.name: Yuval Shalev, Zifeng Ding, Mateja Jamnik

entry.summary: Introduces In-context Training (ICT) framework for evaluating cross-task self-improvement in language agents, where a reflector model generates system prompts from actor trajectories to improve performance on future unseen tasks, trained via RL.

entry.title: Score-Based Causal Discovery of Latent Variable Causal Models

author.name: Ignavier Ng, Xinshuai Dong, Haoyue Dai, Biwei Huang, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: Develops score-based methods for causal discovery with latent variables, addressing limitations of constraint-based methods like testing-order dependency and error propagation. Extends GES-style approaches to latent variable settings.

entry.title: HealthCraft: A Reinforcement Learning Safety Environment for Emergency Medicine

author.name: Brandon Dent

entry.summary: Introduces HealthCraft, a reinforcement learning environment for evaluating LLM safety in emergency medicine scenarios. Built on FHIR R4 with 14 entity types, 24 MCP tools, and 195 tasks with a dual-layer safety rubric.

entry.title: Two is better than one: A Collapse-free Multi-Reward RLIF Training Framework

author.name: Shourov Joarder, Diganta Sikdar, Ahsan Habib Akash, Binod Bhattarai, Prashnna Gyawali

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-reward RLIF (reinforcement learning from internal feedback) framework combining cluster voting (answer-level) and token-wise self-certainty (completion-level) rewards to prevent collapse in unsupervised RL training.

entry.title: Hierarchical Variational Policies for Reward-Guided Diffusion

author.name: Kushagra Pandey, Farrin Marouf Sofian, Jan Niklas Groeneveld, Felix Draxler, Stephan Mandt

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical variational framework for adapting pretrained diffusion models to downstream objectives by amortizing control into a lightweight stochastic policy. Enables few-step sampling while maintaining quality through structured per-step control.

entry.title: Uniform-in-Time Weak Propagation-of-Chaos in Shallow Neural Networks

author.name: Margalit Glasgow, Joan Bruna

entry.summary: Establishes non-asymptotic weak propagation-of-chaos bounds that hold uniformly in time for one-hidden-layer neural networks in the feature-learning (mean-field) regime, relating finite-width to infinite-width dynamics without requiring strong convexity or noise.

entry.title: Conflict-Aware Additive Guidance for Flow Models under Compositional Rewards

author.name: Xuehui Yu, Fucheng Cai, Meiyi Wang, Xiaopeng Fan, Harold Soh

entry.summary: Proposes Conflict-Aware Additive Guidance (g^car) for flow/diffusion models that addresses off-manifold drift when composing multiple constraints during inference-time guided sampling. Identifies that approximation error scales with gradient misalignment.

entry.title: Playing Devil's Advocate: Off-the-Shelf Persona Vectors Rival Targeted Steering for Sycophancy

author.name: Ishaan Kelkar, Nebras Alam, Vikram Kakaria, Madhur Panwar, Vasu Sharma, Maheep Chaudhary

entry.summary: Shows that off-the-shelf persona steering vectors (e.g., 'doubtful' personas) can reduce sycophancy in LLMs nearly as effectively as targeted Contrastive Activation Addition, while better maintaining accuracy when users are correct.

entry.title: FlowLM: Few-Step Language Modeling via Diffusion-to-Flow Adaptation

author.name: Runzhe Zhang, Letian Chen, Wenpeng Zhang, Zhouhan Lin, Peilin Zhao

entry.summary: FlowLM transforms pre-trained diffusion language models into flow matching models via efficient fine-tuning, enabling few-step generation that rivals 2000-step diffusion sampling quality with minimal training.

entry.title: Can Vision Models Truly Forget? Mirage: Representation-Level Certification of Visual Unlearning

author.name: Zhenyu Yu, Yangchen Zeng, Chunlei Meng, Guangzhen Yao, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: Mirage introduces a representation-level auditing framework for machine unlearning in Vertical Federated Learning, revealing that methods passing output-level certification still retain substantial class structure internally.

entry.title: Closed-form predictive coding via hierarchical Gaussian filters

author.name: Aleksandrs Baskakovs, Sylvain Estebe, Kenneth Enevoldsen, Kristoffer Nielbo, Chris Mathys, Nicolas Legrand

entry.summary: Connects predictive coding networks to hierarchical Gaussian filters, restoring precision-weighted message passing that current PC networks omit. This yields dynamic uncertainty estimates and Hebbian-compatible update rules, enabling closed-form (non-iterative) inference at each layer.

entry.title: Synchronization and Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Speech Dialogue Models

author.name: Pablo Riera, Pablo Brusco, Cristina Kuo, Marcelo Sancinetti, S. R. K. Branavan

entry.summary: Studies synchronization and turn-taking in full-duplex spoken dialogue models by simulating dialogues between two Moshi model instances and measuring representational synchronization using CKA. Finds strong coupling patterns analogous to neural coupling in human communication.

entry.title: SUGAR: A Scalable Human-Video-Driven Generalizable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation Learning Framework

author.name: Tianshu Wu, Xiangqi Kong, Yue Chen, Qize Yu, Hang Ye, Jia Li, Yizhou Wang, Hao Dong

entry.summary: SUGAR is a scalable framework that converts diverse human videos into deployable humanoid robot loco-manipulation skills without task-specific reward engineering, handling imperfect motion priors from videos through a data-driven approach.

entry.title: LLM Pretraining Shapes a Generalizable Manifold: Insights into Cross-Modal Transfer to Time Series

author.name: Alexis Roger, Prateek Humane, Zhenghan Tai, Gwen Legate, Andrei Mircea, Vasilii Feofanov, Irina Rish

entry.summary: Shows that language-pretrained transformers transfer to time series forecasting because LLM pretraining creates a reusable manifold. A linear probe on frozen LLM states decodes realistic time-series without paired supervision, and finetuning acts as low-dimensional alignment.

entry.title: Code Generation by Differential Test Time Scaling

author.name: Yifeng He, Ethan Wang, Jicheng Wang, Xuanxin Ouyang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: DiffCodeGen uses coverage-guided differential analysis for test-time scaling in code generation, synthesizing test inputs via fuzzing without requiring existing tests or LLM calls for candidate selection, then identifying correct solutions through behavioral divergence.

entry.title: Rethinking Cross-Layer Information Routing in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Chao Xu, Maohua Li, Qirui Li, Yixuan Xu, Yanke Zhou, Yunhe Li, Cuifeng Shen, Hanlin Tang, Kan Liu, Tao Lan, Lin Qu, Shao-Qun Zhang

entry.summary: Systematically analyzes cross-layer information flow in Diffusion Transformers, identifies three pathologies of standard residual connections (magnitude inflation, gradient decay, block redundancy), and proposes improved routing mechanisms.

entry.title: Terminal-World: Scaling Terminal-Agent Environments via Agent Skills

author.name: Zihao Cheng, Hongru Wang, Zeming Liu, Xinyi Wang, Xiangrong Zhu, Yuhang Guo, Wei Lin, Jeff Z. Pan, Yunhong Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Terminal-World, a fully automated pipeline using agent skills as synthesis primitives to generate high-quality training data for terminal/command-line agents, addressing the scarcity of training data.

entry.title: Finding the Correct Visual Evidence Without Forgetting: Mitigating Hallucination in LVLMs via Inter-Layer Visual Attention Discrepancy

author.name: Yutong Xie, Zhenglin Hua, Ran Wang, Wing W. Y. Ng, Xizhao Wang, Yuheng Jia

entry.summary: Proposes a hallucination mitigation method for Large Vision-Language Models based on inter-layer visual attention discrepancy, finding that LVLMs show sensitivity to correct visual evidence in specific layers despite overall insufficient attention.

entry.title: A Sharper Picture of Generalization in Transformers

author.name: Paul Lintilhac, Sair Shaikh

entry.summary: Studies transformer generalization on boolean domains via PAC-Bayes theory, showing that sparse Fourier spectra concentrated on low-degree components enable flat minima with good generalization properties.

entry.title: OCTOPUS: Optimized KV Cache for Transformers via Octahedral Parametrization Under optimal Squared error quantization

author.name: Mark Boss, Vikram Voleti, Simon Donn\'e, Shimon Vainer

entry.summary: OCTOPUS advances KV cache compression through joint quantization of rotated coordinate triplets using octahedral parameterization, achieving non-uniform bit allocation that outperforms per-coordinate quantizers.

entry.title: Lost in Fog: Sensor Perturbations Expose Reasoning Fragility in Driving VLAs

author.name: Abhinaw Priyadershi, Jelena Frtunikj

entry.summary: Studies robustness of Vision-Language-Action models for autonomous driving under sensor perturbations. Finds that reasoning consistency (Chain-of-Causation explanations) is a high-fidelity indicator of trajectory reliability, with 5.3x trajectory deviation spike when explanations change.

entry.title: Variance Reduction for Expectations with Diffusion Teachers

author.name: Jesse Bettencourt, Xindi Wu, Matan Atzmon, James Lucas, Jonathan Lorraine

entry.summary: Introduces CARV, a compute-aware variance reduction framework for diffusion model teacher gradients used in text-to-3D and distillation. Proposes hierarchical MC estimator that amortizes expensive upstream computation over cheap noise resamples.

entry.title: Distributed Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Zhanhong Jiang

entry.summary: Provides first convergence and time-complexity analysis of DPO in distributed (federated and decentralized) settings with non-IID preferences. Establishes theoretical guarantees for distributed preference optimization.

entry.title: Training distribution determines the ceiling of drug-blind cancer sensitivity prediction

author.name: Taekyung Heo

entry.summary: Shows that drug-blind cancer sensitivity prediction has plateaued due to a metric artifact (global Pearson r dominated by between-drug potency differences). Per-drug evaluation reveals no drug encoding improves over cell-only features.

entry.title: A Dialogue between Causal and Traditional Representation Learning: Toward Mutual Benefits in a Unified Formulation

author.name: Yan Li, Yuewen Sun, Shaoan Xie, Gongxu Luo, Yunlong Deng, Kun Zhang, Guangyi Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a unified formulation bridging causal representation learning and traditional representation learning, arguing these two fields should be in dialogue. Introduces a framework where representation learning is characterized by two core components to facilitate cross-pollination.

entry.title: HORST: Composing Optimizer Geometries for Sparse Transformer Training

author.name: Tom Jacobs, Rohan Jain, Rebekka Burkholz

entry.summary: Proposes HORST, a modular optimizer that composes L∞ stability from adaptive methods with L1 sparsity bias through hyperbolic mirror maps for sparse Transformer training. Frames optimizer composition as non-commutative operators.

entry.title: Graph Navier Stokes Networks

author.name: Zexing Zhao, Guangsi Shi, Yu Gong, Tianyu Wang, Shirui Pan, Hongye Cheng, Yuxiao Li

entry.summary: Introduces Graph Navier-Stokes Networks that incorporate convection from fluid dynamics into GNN message passing, addressing oversmoothing by defining dynamic velocity fields on graphs to govern information propagation.

entry.title: What Twelve LLM Agent Benchmark Papers Disclose About Themselves: A Pilot Audit and an Open Scoring Schema

author.name: Mahdi Naser Moghadasi (BrightMind AI, Texas Tech University), Faezeh Ghaderi (University of Texas at Arlington)

entry.summary: Audits 12 LLM agent benchmark papers using a structured schema to assess reproducibility and reporting quality, revealing widespread gaps in harness specification, inference settings, and cost reporting.

entry.title: Adaptive Probe-based Steering for Robust LLM Jailbreaking

author.name: Junxi Chen, Junhao Dong, Xiaohua Xie

entry.summary: Proposes adaptive probe-based steering for LLM jailbreaking that uses model extraction to approximate ideal steering vectors and adaptively tunes steering strength, improving attack effectiveness without manual tuning.

entry.title: Contradiction Graphs Determine VC Dimension

author.name: Jesse Campbell, Daniel Ibaibarriaga, Lev Reyzin

entry.summary: Proves that contradiction graphs determine VC dimension: the order-m contradiction graph G_m(H) determines whether VCdim(H)≥m, answering a question posed by Alon et al. (2024).

entry.title: Sample Complexity of Transfer Learning: An Optimal Transport Approach

author.name: Haoyang Cao, Xin Guo, Wenpin Tang, Guan Wang

entry.summary: Provides rigorous analysis of transfer learning sample complexity using optimal transport, showing that for data dimension d>3, transfer learning achieves O(m^{-(α+1)/d}) sample complexity improvement over learning from scratch.

entry.title: RoPeSLR: 3D RoPE-driven Sparse-LowRank Attention for Efficient Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Yuxi Liu, Zekun Zhang, Yixiang Cai, Renjia Deng, Yutong He, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes RoPeSLR addressing the 'RoPE Dilemma' in Diffusion Transformers where sparse-linear attention hybrids fail to preserve 3D rotary position embeddings, enabling efficient long-sequence video generation.

entry.title: Everywhere Valid Bounds on False Discovery Proportions in Conformal Inference

author.name: Ziang Song, Ying Jin, Emmanuel J. Cand\`es

entry.summary: Establishes finite-sample, distribution-free upper bounds on false discovery proportion in conformal inference for multiple testing, providing high-probability guarantees rather than just expected FDP control.

entry.title: Activation-Free Backbones for Image Recognition: Polynomial Alternatives within MetaFormer-Style Vision Models

author.name: Jeffrey Wang, Jonathan Gregory, Grigorios G. Chrysos

entry.summary: Demonstrates that activation functions (ReLU, GELU, softmax) are not necessary in MetaFormer-style vision backbones, replacing them with polynomial alternatives using Hadamard products while matching performance on ImageNet and ADE20K.

entry.title: Stimulus symmetries can confound representational similarity analyses

author.name: Farhad Pashakhanloo, Jacob A. Zavatone-Veth

entry.summary: Shows that stimulus symmetries in neural networks can confound representational similarity matrix analyses, with stochastic gradient descent generating drifting codes that lead to qualitatively different RSMs for functionally equivalent representations.

entry.title: roto 2.0: The Robot Tactile Olympiad

author.name: Elle Miller, Jayaram Reddy, Ayush Deshmukh, Trevor McInroe, David Abel, Oisin Mac Aodha, Sethu Vijayakumar

entry.summary: Introduces roto 2.0, a GPU-parallelized benchmark for tactile-based RL across four robotic morphologies, achieving 13 Baoding ball rotations in 10 seconds using only proprioception and tactile sensing without vision.

entry.title: Probabilistic Attribution For Large Language Models

author.name: Shilpika Shilpika, Carlo Graziani, Bethany Lusch, Venkatram Vishwanath, Michael E. Papka

entry.summary: Develops a model-agnostic probabilistic token attribution measure for LLMs using Bayes rule to invert next-token log-probabilities, situating LLMs within stochastic process theory to capture internal distributional representations.

entry.title: PromptNCE: Pointwise Mutual Information Predictions Using Only LLMs and Contrastive Estimation Prompts

author.name: Juliette Woodrow, Chris Piech

entry.summary: Introduces PromptNCE, a method for zero-shot pointwise mutual information estimation using only LLM prompts and elicited probabilities, with an explicit OTHER category that recovers true conditional probabilities rather than just rankings.

entry.title: Hy-MT2: A Family of Fast, Efficient and Powerful Multilingual Translation Models in the Wild

author.name: Mao Zheng, Zheng Li, Tao Chen, Bo Lv, Mingrui Sun, Mingyang Song, Jinlong Song, Hong Huang, Decheng Wu, Hai Wang, Yifan Song, Yanfeng Chen, Guanwei Zhang, Guanghua Yu, Yi Su, Hong Liu, Jinxiang Ou, Keyao Wang, Weile Chen, Haozhao Kuang, Kai Wang, Nuo Chen, Zihao Zheng, Chenhao Wang, Bin Xing, Chengcheng Xu, Tinghao Yu, Binghong Wu, Long Xu, Jiacheng Shi, Yunhao Wang, Baifang Chen, Lei Zhang, Qi Yang, Zhao Wu, Jiacheng Li, Lan Jiang, Lanrui Wang, Kai Zhang, Shuaipeng Li, Zhongzhi Chen, Weixuan Sun, Jiaqi Zhu, An Wang, Wei Li, Jun Xia, Weidong Han, Wutian Yang, Litong Hui, Luoguo Jia, Jiajia Wu, Xinpeng Zhou, Tianxiang Fei

entry.summary: Presents Hy-MT2, a family of multilingual translation models (1.8B, 7B, 30B-MoE) supporting 33 languages with extreme quantization for on-device deployment. Claims to outperform DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Kimi K2.6 in fast-thinking translation mode.

entry.title: LANG: Reinforcement Learning for Multilingual Reasoning with Language-Adaptive Hint Guidance

author.name: Yuchun Fan, Bei Li, Peiguang Li, Yilin Wang, Yongyu Mu, Jian Yang, Xin Chen, Rongxiang Weng, Jingang Wang, Xunliang Cai, Jingbo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes LANG, a framework using language-conditioned hints with progressive decay and language-adaptive switching to improve multilingual reasoning in LLMs via RL, addressing the language-reasoning trade-off.

entry.title: ChronoMedKG: A Temporally-Grounded Biomedical Knowledge Graph and Benchmark for Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Md Shamim Ahmed, Farzaneh Firoozbakht, Lukas Galke Poech, Jan Baumbach, Richard R\"ottger

entry.summary: Introduces ChronoMedKG, a temporal biomedical knowledge graph with 460K evidence-linked triples covering 13K diseases, where each association is tied to onset windows or progression stages. Addresses the limitation that existing KGs treat disease associations as static.

entry.title: X-Token: Projection-Guided Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Sharath Turuvekere Sreenivas, Adithyakrishna Venkatesh Hanasoge, Mingyu Yang, Ali Taghibakhshi, Saurav Muralidharan, Ashwath Aithal, Pavlo Molchanov

entry.summary: Proposes X-Token for cross-tokenizer knowledge distillation using projection-guided methods. Addresses failures of full-distribution logit methods (uncommon-token failure, soft-target collapse) with a learned projection approach.

entry.title: Boundary-targeted Membership Inference Attacks on Safety Classifiers

author.name: Anthony Hughes, Alexander Goldberg, Prince Jha, Adam Perer, Nikolaos Aletras, Niloofar Mireshghallah

entry.summary: Proposes boundary-targeted membership inference attacks on safety classifiers, exploiting the insight that examples near the decision boundary are most informative for inferring training set membership.

entry.title: PhysX-Omni: Unified Simulation-Ready Physical 3D Generation for Rigid, Deformable, and Articulated Objects

author.name: Ziang Cao, Yinghao Liu, Haitian Li, Runmao Yao, Fangzhou Hong, Zhaoxi Chen, Liang Pan, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: Introduces PhysX-Omni, a unified framework for generating simulation-ready 3D assets (rigid, deformable, articulated) with physical properties. Develops efficient geometry representation for VLMs and constructs the first general sim-ready 3D dataset.

entry.title: Video as Natural Augmentation: Towards Unified AI-Generated Image and Video Detection

author.name: Zhengcen Li, Chenyang Jiang, Liangxu Su, Tong Shao, Shiyang Zhou, Ming Tao, Jingyong Su

entry.summary: VINA identifies that SOTA AI-generated image detectors fail on video frames due to codec compression, color conversion, and model-specific fingerprints. It proposes using video as natural augmentation to bridge this cross-modal gap for unified AI-generated content detection.

entry.title: ForeSplat: Optimization-Aware Foresight for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yuke Li, Weihang Liu, Cheng Zhang, Yuefeng Zhang, Jiadi Cui, Zixuan Wang, Junran Ding, Haoyu Wu, Yujiao Shi, Jingyi Yu, Xin Lou

entry.summary: ForeSplat introduces optimization-aware training for feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting, producing initializations explicitly designed for rapid refinement rather than just minimizing zero-step rendering error. Bridges the gap between fast feed-forward prediction and quality per-scene optimization.

entry.title: No Pose, No Problem in 4D: Feed-Forward Dynamic Gaussians from Unposed Multi-View Videos

author.name: Matteo Balice, Yanik Kunzi, Chenyangguang Zhang, Matteo Matteucci, Marc Pollefeys, Sungwhan Hong

entry.summary: NoPo4D is the first feed-forward system that jointly addresses dynamic content, multi-view input, and unknown camera poses in a single forward pass for 4D Gaussian Splatting, using velocity decomposition to split Gaussian motion.

entry.title: Pre-VLA: Preemptive Runtime Verification for Reliable Vision-Language-Action and World-Model Rollouts

author.name: Zhen Sun, Yongjian Guo, Haoran Sun, Luqiao Wang, Wei Lu, Jiachi Ji, Shengzhe Ji, Junwu Xiong, Zhijun Meng

entry.summary: Pre-VLA proposes preemptive runtime verification for VLA models and world models, assessing action validity before physical execution to prevent failures, using a lightweight dual-branch head predicting safety confidence and advantage scores.

entry.title: GeoWeaver: Grounding Visual Tokens with Geometric Evidence before Scene Reasoning

author.name: Deshui Miao, Xingsen Huang, Yameng Gu, Xin Li, Haijun Zhang, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: Introduces GeoWeaver, a pre-reasoning geometric grounding framework for vision-language models that assigns different geometric evidence to different visual tokens based on their spatial roles. Addresses the limitation of treating geometric cues as shared signals across all tokens.

entry.title: SegCompass: Exploring Interpretable Alignment with Sparse Autoencoders for Enhanced Reasoning Segmentation

author.name: Zhenyu Lu, Liupeng Li, Jinpeng Wang, Haoqian Kang, Yan Feng, Ke Chen, Yaowei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes SegCompass, which uses a Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) to create an explicit, interpretable alignment pathway between chain-of-thought reasoning and visual segmentation. Bridges the interpretability gap between opaque end-to-end methods and readable but unconstrained text-based approaches.

entry.title: Dropout Universality: Scaling Laws and Optimal Scheduling at the Edge-of-Chaos

author.name: Lucas Fernandez Sarmiento

entry.summary: Develops mean-field theory of dropout as a perturbation at the edge of chaos, deriving critical scaling laws and showing smooth vs. ReLU-like activations form distinct universality classes. Derives an optimal dropout schedule from the theory.

entry.title: PGDG: Physically Grounded Data Generation for Robust Bimanual Policy Learning from a Single Demonstration

author.name: Cunxi Dai, Haoran Chang, Aditya Nisal, Rahul Kumar, Guofei Chen, Tao Chen, Yuzhe Qin, Guanya Shi

entry.summary: Proposes PGDG, a physically grounded data generation framework that expands a single demonstration into diverse recovery behaviors for bimanual manipulation through physics-grounded sampling and zero-shot curation without human labeling.

entry.title: Action with Visual Primitives

author.name: Weilong Guo, Yuchen Wang, Renping Zhou, Yunfeng Zhang, Rui Fang, Yue Meng, Wenda Xu, Yuan He, Gao Huang

entry.summary: Introduces AVP (Action with Visual Primitives), a VLA architecture that decouples instruction comprehension and spatial understanding from motor control. The VLM infers visual primitives that serve as an interface to the action expert, avoiding redundant relearning of perceptual capabilities.

entry.title: Symmetries Here and There, Combined Everywhere: Cross-space Symmetry Compositions in Robotics

author.name: Loizos Hadjiloizou, Rodrigo P\'erez-Dattari, No\'emie Jaquier

entry.summary: Introduces cross-space symmetry compositions, a framework for learning robot policies that are jointly equivariant to multiple symmetries across configuration and task spaces by leveraging the differential-geometric structure of forward kinematics.

entry.title: Robust Statistical Estimators with Bounded Empirical Sensitivity

author.name: Valentio Iverson, Gautam Kamath, Argyris Mouzakis, Adam Smith

entry.summary: Introduces empirical sensitivity as a robustness measure for statistical estimators, proving lower bounds showing optimal Gaussian mean estimators must have sensitivity at least Ω(η + √(ηd/n)), and providing matching upper bounds via a novel sum-of-squares estimator.

entry.title: Uniform Diffusion Models Revisited: Leave-One-Out Denoiser and Absorbing State Reformulation

author.name: Samson Gourevitch, Yazid Janati, Dario Shariatian, Umut Simsekli, Eric Moulines, Eric P. Xing, Alain Durmus

entry.summary: Shows that the standard plug-in parameterization for Uniform Diffusion Models is not optimized by the denoising posterior but by a leave-one-out posterior, identifying a mismatch between ELBO and cross-entropy objectives. Derives exact conversions between denoiser, leave-one-out posterior, and score.

entry.title: AI #169: New Knowledge

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's AI newsletter covering OpenAI's math result (unit distance problem), METR's risk report on frontier models, Andrej Karpathy joining Anthropic for recursive self-improvement, Musk's case dismissal, and other AI developments.

entry.title: Swift Sampling: Selecting Temporal Surprises via Taylor Series

author.name: Dahye Kim, Bhuvan Sachdeva, Karan Uppal, Naman Gupta, Vineeth N. Balasubramanian, Deepti Ghadiyaram

entry.summary: Introduces Swift Sampling, a training-free frame selection algorithm inspired by predictive coding that identifies high-information moments in video using Taylor expansion to predict expected feature trajectories and select frames that deviate from predictions.

entry.title: Safe and Steerable Geometric Motion Policies for Robotic Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Albert Wu, Riccardo Bonalli, Thomas Lew, C. Karen Liu

entry.summary: Presents SafePBDS, a geometrically consistent framework for dexterous manipulation that computes certifiably safe accelerations from objectives and constraints on arbitrary task manifolds using pullback control barrier functions.

entry.title: It Takes Two: Complementary Self-Distillation for Contextual Integrity in LLMs

author.name: Sangwoo Park, Woongyeong Yeo, Seanie Lee, Yumin Choi, Hyomin Lee, Kangsan Kim, Jinheon Baek, Seong Joon Oh, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: SELFCI proposes complementary self-distillation to balance privacy (contextual integrity) and utility in LLM personal agents, decoupling information suppression from task resolution through dual reverse KL objectives.

entry.title: Learning to Think in Physics: Breaking Shortcut Learning in Scientific Diffusion via Representation Alignment

author.name: Haozhe Jia, Pengyu Yin, Wenshuo Chen, Shaofeng Liang, Lei Wang, Bowen Tian, Xiucheng Wang, Nanqian Jia, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: Introduces REPA-P, a teacher-free framework that aligns intermediate diffusion model features with physical states using PDE residual losses during training, preventing shortcut learning under shifted boundary conditions. Zero inference overhead.

entry.title: Markovian Circuit Tracing for Transformer State Dynamic

author.name: Abdullah X

entry.summary: Introduces Markovian Circuit Tracing (MCT), a diagnostic pipeline testing whether transformer activations contain coarse state-transition structure using synthetic HMM tasks with known ground truth.

entry.title: Planning in the LLM Era: Building for Reliability and Efficiency

author.name: Michael Katz, Harsha Kokel, Kavitha Srinivas, Shirin Sohrabi

entry.summary: Surveys the evolution of LLM-based planning from single-shot generation to hybrid approaches to generating symbolic solvers. Argues for reliable, verifiable planning through solver synthesis rather than direct LLM planning.

entry.title: Conceptualizing Embeddings: Sparse Disentanglement for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Piotr Kubaty, Patryk Marsza{\l}ek, {\L}ukasz Struski, Adam Wr\'obel, Jacek Tabor, Marek \'Smieja

entry.summary: Introduces CEDAR, a post-hoc method that reveals compositional structure of pretrained VLM embeddings through an invertible rotation with sparsity bottleneck, achieving disentanglement without increasing dimensionality, unlike sparse autoencoders.

entry.title: EvoScene-VLA: Evolving Scene Beliefs Inside the Action Decoder for Chunked Robot Control

author.name: Chushan Zhang, Ruihan Lu, Jinguang Tong, Xuesong Li, Yikai Wang, Hongdong Li

entry.summary: Introduces EvoScene-VLA with a recurrent scene prefix that maintains action-updated scene state across control chunks, addressing the gap where neither spatial nor temporal VLAs maintain persistent scene beliefs that evolve with robot actions.

entry.title: $ECUAS_n$: A family of metrics for principled evaluation of uncertainty-augmented systems

author.name: Lautaro Estienne, Erik Ernst, Mat\'ias Vera, Pablo Piantanida, Luciana Ferrer

entry.summary: Proposes ECUAS_n, a family of metrics for evaluating uncertainty-augmented systems that output both predictions and uncertainty scores. Argues existing evaluation approaches are inadequate for assessing decision-making under uncertainty.

entry.title: PALS: Power-Aware LLM Serving for Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Can Hankendi, Rana Shahout, Minlan Yu, Ayse K. Coskun

entry.summary: PALS treats GPU power caps as a first-class control knob for LLM serving of MoE models, combining offline power-performance models with feedback-driven controllers to maximize energy efficiency while meeting throughput targets.

entry.title: GrandGuard: Taxonomy, Benchmark, and Safeguards for Elderly-Chatbot Interaction Safety

author.name: Changxuan Fan, Xi Yang, Yueyuan Zheng, Bin Zhou, Yuanping Wang, Wenbin Hu, Huihao Jing, Ki Sen Hung, Dazhao Du, Haoran Li, Janet Hui-wen Hsiao, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: GrandGuard introduces the first comprehensive framework for elderly-specific AI safety risks, with a three-level taxonomy of 50 risk types and safeguard mechanisms for LLM chatbot interactions with older adults.

entry.title: GROW: Aligning GRPO with State-Action Modeling for Open-World VLM Agents

author.name: Xiongbin Wu, Zhihao Luo, Shanzhe Lei, Lechao Zhang, Xuhong Wang, Jie Yang, Zhonglong Zheng, Yuanjie Zheng, Xin Tan, Wei Liu

entry.summary: GROW adapts GRPO for multi-turn RL in open-world VLM agents by decomposing trajectories into state-action samples, avoiding the excessively long context problem of standard GRPO on full trajectories.

entry.title: Chronicle: A Multimodal Foundation Model for Joint Language and Time Series Understanding

author.name: Paul Quinlan, Jeremy Levasseur, Qingguo Li, Xiaodan Zhu

entry.summary: Chronicle is a 324M-parameter transformer trained from scratch on both language and time series in a unified architecture, sharing representations across modalities. Claims advantages over post-hoc multimodal adaptations.

entry.title: Smaller Abstract State Spaces Enable Cross-Scale Generalization in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nasehatul Mustakim, Lucas Lehnert

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical model of out-of-distribution generalization in RL via smaller abstract state spaces, extending state abstraction to POMDPs and defining successor-weighted model reductions that enable cross-scale transfer.

entry.title: Quant.npu: Enabling Efficient Mobile NPU Inference for on-device LLMs via Fully Static Quantization

author.name: Jinghe Zhang, Daliang Xu, Chenghua Wang, Weikai Xie, Tao Qi, Yun Ma, Mengwei Xu, Gang Huang

entry.summary: Quant.npu is a fully static quantization framework for LLMs on mobile NPUs, using learnable quantization parameters and rotation matrices to enable low-bit inference without runtime re-computation. Addresses the incompatibility between existing dynamic PTQ methods and NPU hardware constraints.

entry.title: Mechanisms of Misgeneralization in Physical Sequence Modeling

author.name: Kento Nishi, Raphael Tang, Karun Kumar, Core Francisco Park, Hidenori Tanaka

entry.summary: Identifies 'physical misgeneralization' where sequence models trained on curated demonstrations produce individually plausible trajectories but aggregate distributions over physical quantities (distance, energy) are wrong. Provides mechanistic analysis of this failure mode in robotics/simulation domains.

entry.title: REFLECTOR: Internalizing Step-wise Reflection against Indirect Jailbreak

author.name: Jiachen Ma, Jiawen Zhang, Xiangtian Li, Bo Zou, Chaochao Lu, Chao Yang

entry.summary: REFLECTOR internalizes step-wise self-reflection against indirect jailbreak attacks through teacher-guided SFT followed by RL with outcome-driven supervision, embedding safety reflection within the generation trajectory.

entry.title: An Application-Layer Multi-Modal Covert-Channel Reference Monitor for LLM Agent Egress

author.name: Alfredo Metere

entry.summary: Proposes a reference monitor for detecting covert channels in LLM agent communications, addressing data exfiltration via techniques like zero-width characters, homoglyphs, timing channels, and steganography. The system uses a ten-stage text pipeline with capacity-reducing stages and per-sink rate limiting.

entry.title: Sutra: Tensor-Op RNNs as a Compilation Target for Vector Symbolic Architectures

author.name: Emma Leonhart

entry.summary: Sutra is a typed functional programming language whose programs compile to PyTorch neural network forward passes, using vector symbolic architectures with operations over frozen embeddings spanning text and protein modalities.

entry.title: Decoupling Communication from Policy: Robust MARL under Bandwidth Constraints

author.name: Alexi Canesse, Beno\^it Goupil, Jesse Read, Sonia Vanier

entry.summary: Addresses bandwidth-constrained multi-agent RL by decoupling communication from policy representation, introducing a normalized bandwidth budget metric and SLIM architecture that separates message encoding from policy latent space.

entry.title: Detecting Trojaned DNNs via Spectral Regression Analysis

author.name: Samuele Pasini, Jinhan Kim, Paolo Tonella

entry.summary: Presents MIST, a Trojan detection approach that analyzes spectral changes in model representations during fine-tuning, treating Trojan detection as a regression problem over model updates rather than trigger reconstruction.

entry.title: PREFINE: Preference-Based Implicit Reward and Cost Fine-Tuning for Safety Alignment

author.name: Richa Verma, Bavish Kulur, Sanjay Chawla, Balaraman Ravindran

entry.summary: Introduces PREFINE for fine-tuning RL policies with safety constraints expressed as trajectory-level preferences, allowing incorporation of cost constraints without retraining from scratch.

entry.title: Tracing the ongoing emergence of human-like reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Paolo Morosi, Nikoleta Pantelidou, Fritz G\"unther, Elena Pagliarini, Evelina Leivada

entry.summary: Tests 25 LLMs on conditional inference computation across four languages, finding that model behavior is increasingly human-like with scale and that pragmatic enrichment emerges progressively.

entry.title: TextReg: Mitigating Prompt Distributional Overfitting via Regularized Text-Space Optimization

author.name: Lucheng Fu, Ye Yu, Yiyang Wang, Yiqiao Jin, Haibo Jin, B. Aditya Prakash, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: Studies prompt distributional overfitting in LLM prompt optimization, formalizing it through representational inefficiency and proposing TextReg to regularize text-space optimization.

entry.title: Stdlib or Third-Party? Empirical Performance and Correctness of LLM-Assisted Zero-Dependency Python Libraries

author.name: Peng Ding, Rick Stevens

entry.summary: Empirically evaluates LLM-assisted reimplementations of 40+ popular Python libraries using only the standard library (zerodep project). Tests correctness and performance against reference implementations under strict constraints. Addresses supply chain security and dependency management concerns.

entry.title: Neural Collapse by Design: Learning Class Prototypes on the Hypersphere

author.name: Panagiotis Koromilas, Theodoros Giannakopoulos, Mihalis A. Nicolaou, Yannis Panagakis

entry.summary: Shows that cross-entropy and supervised contrastive learning are different views of the same prototype-contrasting method on the hypersphere. Proposes normalized losses (NTCE, NONL) that achieve neural collapse in practice.

entry.title: ZEBRA: Zero-shot Budgeted Resource Allocation for LLM Orchestration

author.name: May Hamri, Inbal Talgam-Cohen

entry.summary: Proposes ZEBRA, a zero-shot framework for allocating budgets across phases of multi-agent LLM pipelines by reducing it to a continuous nonlinear knapsack problem with LLM-estimated utility curves.

entry.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Learning Assurance of a Vision-Based Landing System

author.name: Romeo Valentin, Olivia Beyer Bruvik, Marc R. Schlichting, Mykel J. Kochenderfer

entry.summary: Proposes using mechanistic interpretability for learning assurance of vision-based aircraft landing systems, demonstrating that models should separate content from style in their representations per EASA guidance.

entry.title: Beyond the Bellman Recursion: A Pontryagin-Guided Framework for Non-Exponential Discounting

author.name: Hojin Ko, Jeonggyu Huh

entry.summary: Proposes PG-DPO, a variational framework using Pontryagin Maximum Principle instead of Bellman recursions for RL with non-exponential discounting (e.g., hyperbolic). Shows that standard dynamic programming fundamentally breaks under non-exponential discounting and provides an alternative via Monte Carlo rollouts with adjoint projections.

entry.title: Learning First Integrals via Backward-Generated Data and Guided Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jingfeng Zhong, Zhengxiang Liu, Zhijie Wang, Shuai Li

entry.summary: Presents FISolver, an LLM-based solver for discovering first integrals of dynamical systems. Uses a 'Backward Generation' algorithm to create training data and applies RL with guided Monte Carlo Tree Search for complex problems.

entry.title: Polynomial-Time Robust Multiclass Linear Classification under Gaussian Marginals

author.name: Ilias Diakonikolas, Giannis Iakovidis, Mingchen Ma

entry.summary: Develops polynomial-time robust algorithms for multiclass linear classification under Gaussian marginals, overcoming prior exponential dependence on inverse accuracy for k≥3 classes.

entry.title: Mitigating Label Bias with Interpretable Rubric Embeddings

author.name: Calvin Isley, Johann D. Gaebler, Sharad Goel

entry.summary: Proposes rubric embeddings for mitigating label bias in ML systems used for decisions like hiring and admissions, replacing black-box features with expert-defined criteria to prevent propagation of historical biases.

entry.title: Instant GPU Efficiency Visibility at Fleet Scale

author.name: Connor Pedersen, Dong H. Ahn, Michel Migdal, Collin Neale, Nik Konyuchenko

entry.summary: Presents OFU (Overall FLOP Utilization), a hardware-level GPU efficiency metric derived from two performance counters, validated on H100 and GB200 across multiple precisions and 608 production training jobs.

entry.title: Semiparametric Efficient Bilevel Gradient Estimation

author.name: Fares El Khoury, Houssam Zenati, Nathan Kallus, Michael Arbel, Aur\'elien Bibaut

entry.summary: Develops semiparametric debiasing theory for bilevel optimization gradients using efficient influence functions, producing a cross-fitted orthogonal hypergradient estimator with asymptotic normality guarantees.

entry.title: RankJudge: A Multi-Turn LLM-as-a-Judge Synthetic Benchmark Generator

author.name: Zhenwei Tang, Zhaoyan Liu, Rasa Hosseinzadeh, Tongzi Wu, Keyvan Golestan, Jesse C. Cresswell

entry.summary: Introduces RankJudge, a benchmark generator for evaluating LLM-as-a-judge on multi-turn conversations grounded in reference documents, addressing the gap where existing benchmarks focus on simple Q&A.

entry.title: Claim-Selective Certification for High-Risk Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Shao Kan

entry.summary: Studies claim-selective certification for medical RAG systems where responses are decomposed into verifiable claims, scored against evidence, and mapped to actions (full/partial/conflict/abstain) rather than binary answer-or-abstain decisions.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Consensus: Aligning Multilingual Cultural Knowledge via Multilingual Self-Consistency

author.name: Andrew Ivan Soegeng, Patrick Sutanto, Tan Sang Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes a framework using multilingual self-consistency to align cultural knowledge in LLMs, hypothesizing that cultural knowledge exists in local-language representations but fails to surface when prompting in English.

entry.title: DeferMem: Query-Time Evidence Distillation via Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory QA

author.name: Jianing Yin, Tan Tang

entry.summary: Presents DeferMem, a long-term memory QA framework using RL-trained evidence distillation at query time, decoupling high-recall retrieval from query-conditioned evidence extraction for better handling of scattered evidence.

entry.title: Agentic CLEAR: Automating Multi-Level Evaluation of LLM Agents

author.name: Asaf Yehudai, Lilach Eden, Michal Shmueli-Scheuer

entry.summary: Presents Agentic CLEAR, an automatic evaluation framework for LLM agents that provides insights at system, trace, and node levels of granularity. It operates above the observability layer and features dynamic evaluation capabilities rather than static hand-crafted error taxonomies.

entry.title: SpaceDG: Benchmarking Spatial Intelligence under Visual Degradation

author.name: Xiaolong Zhou, Yifei Liu, Ziyang Gong, Jiarui Li, Qiyue Zhao, Muyao Niu, Yuanyuan Gao, Le Ma, Xue Yang, Hongjie Zhang, Zhihang Zhong

entry.summary: Introduces SpaceDG, the first large-scale dataset for degradation-aware spatial understanding in MLLMs. Uses physics-grounded degradation synthesis via 3D Gaussian Splatting to test robustness under motion blur, low light, weather, etc.

entry.title: EvoVid: Temporal-Centric Self-Evolution for Video Large Language Models

author.name: Shiqi Huang, Ziyue Wang, Zhongrong Zuo, Han Qiu, Qi She, Bihan Wen

entry.summary: Proposes EvoVid, a temporal-centric self-evolving framework for Video-LLMs that generates temporally-grounded tasks through autonomous Questioner-Solver self-play, unlike existing approaches designed for static modalities.

entry.title: Rethinking Token Reduction for Diffusion Models via Output-Similarity-Awareness

author.name: Hangyeol Lee, Hyojeong Lee, Joo-Young Kim

entry.summary: DiTo proposes output-centric token reduction for Diffusion Transformers, using output token similarity from previous timesteps rather than input similarity to guide token merging. Shows output similarity is preserved across adjacent timesteps.

entry.title: COCOTree: A Dataset and Benchmark for Open Tree-Structured Visual Decomposition

author.name: Junhyub Lee, Seunghun Chae, Hyosu Kim

entry.summary: COCOTree formalizes open tree decomposition of images into hierarchical component trees, builds a fully automated pipeline combining LVLMs with SAM 3, and constructs a benchmark with 21K images and 1.8M structural nodes with open-vocabulary annotations.

entry.title: OPERA: An Agent for Image Restoration with End-to-End Joint Planning-Execution Optimization

author.name: Feng Zhu, Shuyang Xie, Yihan Zeng, Ming Liu, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: OPERA jointly optimizes restoration planning and tool execution for multi-degradation image restoration using reinforcement learning over a combinatorial plan space, with differentiable fine-tuning of tool parameters to improve coordination.

entry.title: PIU: Proximity-guided Identity Unlearning in ID-Conditioned Diffusion Models

author.name: Jose Edgar Hernandez Cancino Estrada, Mauro D\'iaz Lupone, \v{Z}iga Emer\v{s}i\v{c}, Vitomir \v{S}truc, Peter Peer, Darian Toma\v{s}evi\'c

entry.summary: PIU introduces Proximity-guided Identity Unlearning for identity-conditioned diffusion models like Arc2Face, formulating identity removal as guiding the generation toward nearby but distinct identities to enforce the right to be forgotten.

entry.title: Supervised Classification Heads as Semantic Prototypes: Unlocking Vision-Language Alignment via Weight Recycling

author.name: David M\'endez, Roberto Confalonieri, Natalia D\'iaz Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: Demonstrates that classification head weights from pretrained vision models can serve as semantic prototypes for zero-shot vision-language alignment, enabling cross-modal matching without paired training data by recycling typically discarded parameters.

entry.title: Rethinking Noise-Robust Training for Frozen Vision Foundation Models: A Cross-Dataset Benchmark with a Case Study of Small-Loss Failure

author.name: Zitong Li, Haoyu Wang

entry.summary: Presents a comprehensive benchmark of 8 noisy-label learning methods across 5 medical datasets, 3 backbones, 2 noise types, and 5 noise rates (6,000 training runs) for frozen Vision Foundation Models. Reveals that small-loss assumption fails in the frozen-feature regime.

entry.title: H-Flow: Self-supervised Human Scene Flow via Physics-inspired Joint Multi-modal Learning

author.name: Zhanbo Huang, Xiaoming Liu, Yu Kong

entry.summary: Introduces H-Flow, a self-supervised method for dense human scene flow that captures both skeletal kinematics and surface deformation from monocular video. Uses physics-inspired training objectives encoding geometric, structural, and biomechanical priors instead of ground-truth labels.

entry.title: From Abstraction to Instantiation: Learning Behavioral Representation for Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Bing Hu, Zaijing Li, Rui Shao, Junda Chen, April Hua Liu, Wei-Shi Zheng, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: Proposes BehaviorVLA, a framework for Vision-Language-Action models that learns temporally coherent behavioral representations through a Visuomotor Behavior Encoder, addressing distribution shift failures in existing VLA models.

entry.title: Beyond Pixels: Learning Invariant Rewards for Real-World Robotics From a Few Demonstrations

author.name: Tengye Xu, Yangting Sun, Ziju Shen, Guanqi Chen, Zhen Fu, Chen yizhou, Hua Chen, Jia Pan

entry.summary: Proposes learning invariant symbolic reward functions from as few as five demonstrations for real-world robotics RL. Shifts from visual feature-fitting to discovering behavioral invariants that remain constant across diverse visual conditions.

entry.title: Local Covariate Selection for Average Causal Effect Estimation without Pretreatment and Causal Sufficiency Assumptions

author.name: Zeyu Liu, Zheng Li, Feng Xie, Yan Zeng, Hao Zhang, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a local learning method for covariate selection in causal effect estimation that avoids both pretreatment and causal sufficiency assumptions, which are typically required but unrealistic in practice.

entry.title: A Martingale Kernel Independence Test

author.name: Felix Laumann, Zhaolu Liu, Mauricio Barahona

entry.summary: Introduces a martingale construction for kernel independence testing (mHSIC and mdHSIC) whose null distributions are standard normal regardless of the data law, eliminating the expensive permutation calibration step required by standard HSIC.

entry.title: Generative Modeling by Value-Driven Transport

author.name: Pablo Moreno-Mu\~noz, Adrian M\"uller, Gergely Neu

entry.summary: Proposes value-driven transport (VDT) for generative modeling based on discrete-time stochastic control, formulating the problem as a linear program whose dual gives optimal value functions encoding transport policies. Develops simulation-free primal-dual algorithm.

entry.title: What am I, if not an AI?

author.name: makiba

entry.summary: Experiments RL fine-tuning Mistral 7B and Llama 3.1 8B away from AI self-identification without specifying a target persona. Mistral consistently converged to a single persona (Catholic American woman) while Llama produced diverse working-class personas.

entry.title: MotiMotion: Motion-Controlled Video Generation with Visual Reasoning

author.name: Lee Hsin-Ying, Hanwen Jiang, Yiqun Mei, Jing Shi, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Zhixin Shu

entry.summary: Introduces MotiMotion, which reformulates motion-controlled video generation as a reasoning-then-generation problem, using a vision-language reasoner to refine trajectories and hallucinate secondary causal motions with confidence-aware control.

entry.title: AgentAtlas: Beyond Outcome Leaderboards for LLM Agents

author.name: Parsa Mazaheri, Kasra Mazaheri

entry.summary: AgentAtlas proposes a multi-dimensional evaluation framework for LLM agents beyond simple accuracy, including a six-state control-decision taxonomy, nine-category trajectory-failure taxonomy, and standardized evaluation protocols.

entry.title: Mind the Sim-to-Real Gap & Think Like a Scientist

author.name: Harsh Parikh, Gabriel Levin-Konigsberg, Dominique Perrault-Joncas, Alexander Volfovsky

entry.summary: Studies when a planner should supplement a pre-trained simulator with real experiments, providing an extended simulation lemma decomposing value error and optimal allocation strategies between simulation and experimentation.

entry.title: Neural Estimation of Pairwise Mutual Information in Masked Discrete Sequence Models

author.name: Jai Sharma, Yifan Wang, Bryan Li

entry.summary: Proposes a neural framework for estimating pairwise conditional mutual information from masked diffusion models' hidden states, enabling MI-guided parallel decoding by identifying conditionally independent variable subsets.

entry.title: Lean Refactor: Multi-Objective Controllable Proof Optimization via Agentic Strategy Search

author.name: Jialin Lu, Soonho Kong, Rodrigo Stehling, Kaiyu Yang, Zhangyang Wang, Weiran Sun, Wuyang Chen

entry.summary: Lean Refactor is a retrieval-augmented agentic framework for multi-objective refactoring of Lean proofs (length, compilation cost, version compatibility), working with frozen LLMs across Lean/Mathlib version changes.

entry.title: CP-MoE: Consistency-Preserving Mixture-of-Experts for Continual Learning

author.name: Yang Liu, Toan Nguyen, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: CP-MoE addresses catastrophic forgetting in continual learning with MoE architectures through a transient expert mechanism that captures task-specific updates before integrating them into stable experts with consistency-preserving routing.

entry.title: Conformal Selective Acting: Anytime-Valid Risk Control for RLVR-Trained LLMs

author.name: Hamed Khosravi, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: Proposes conformal selective acting for RLVR-trained LLMs that provides anytime-valid risk control certificates per deployment, addressing gaps in existing conformal methods for adaptive, online-updated streams.

entry.title: Regulating Anatomy-Aware Rewards via Trajectory-Integral Feedback for Volumetric Computed Tomography Analysis

author.name: Tianwei Lin, Zhongwei Qiu, Jie Cao, Jiang Liu, Wenjie Yan, Bo Zhang, Yu Zhong, Wenqiao Zhang, Yingda Xia, Ling Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Clinical Abnormality Benchmarking Substrate (CABS) for CT analysis VLMs, decomposing reports into verifiable clinical units and identifying 'Evaluation Hallucinations' where models optimize fluency over clinical correctness.

entry.title: ClaimDiff-RL: Fine-Grained Caption Reinforcement Learning through Visual Claim Comparison

author.name: Tianle Li, Xuyang Shen, Yan Ma, Rongxin Guo, Shaoxiang Chen, Jiacheng Chen, Haochen Wang, Hongyang Tang, Yucong Zhou, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: ClaimDiff-RL uses reference-conditioned atomic claim differences as the reward unit for caption RL, providing fine-grained feedback at the individual claim level rather than holistic sequence-level rewards.

entry.title: FullFlow: Upgrading Text-to-Image Flow Matching Models for Bidirectional Vision--Language Generation

author.name: Eric Tillmann Bill, Enis Simsar, Alessio Tonioni, Thomas Hofmann

entry.summary: FullFlow upgrades pretrained text-to-image flow matching models into bidirectional vision-language generators by training only LoRA adapters and lightweight text heads, keeping images in continuous flow while adding discrete insertion for text.

entry.title: Decomposing MXFP4 quantization error for LLM reinforcement learning: reducible bias, recoverable deadzone, and an irreducible floor

author.name: Xiaocan Li, Shiliang Wu, Zheng Shen

entry.summary: Proves an exact three-way decomposition of MXFP4 quantization error (scale bias, deadzone truncation, grid noise) and shows how each component damages distinct RL training pathways for LLMs. Provides targeted mitigation strategies.

entry.title: Mechanics of Bias and Reasoning: Interpreting the Impact of Chain-of-Thought Prompting on Gender Bias in LLMs

author.name: Edie Pearman, Sophia Osborne, Mira Kandlikar-Bloch, Mina Arzaghi, Florian Carichon, Golnoosh Farnadi

entry.summary: Investigates how Chain-of-Thought prompting affects gender bias in LLMs using mechanistic interpretability and reasoning chain failure analysis. Finds CoT may produce apparent bias reduction without meaningful internal mechanism changes.

entry.title: NeuroQA: A Large-Scale Image-Grounded Benchmark for 3D Brain MRI Understanding

author.name: Mohammad H. Abbasi (Stanford University), Favour Nerrise (Stanford University), Shaurnav Ghosh (Stanford University), Ridvan Yesiloglu (Stanford University), Yuncong Mao (Stanford University), Bailey Trang (Stanford University), Mohammad Asadi (Stanford University), Merryn Daniel (Stanford University), Gustavo Chau Loo Kung (Stanford University), Ken Chang (Stanford University), Pavan Pinkesh Shah (Stanford University), Adam Turnbull (Stanford University), Kyan Younes (Stanford University), Seena Dehkharghani (Stanford University), Ehsan Adeli (Stanford University)

entry.summary: NeuroQA is a large-scale benchmark for visual question answering on 3D brain MRI with 56,953 QA pairs from 12,977 subjects across 5 clinical domains, evaluating 11 reasoning skills. From Stanford researchers.

entry.title: Jointly Learning Predicates and Actions Enables Zero-Shot Skill Composition

author.name: Benedict Quartey, Sebastian Castro, Eric Rosen, Wil Thomason, George Konidaris, Stefanie Tellex

entry.summary: PACTS jointly models action trajectories and symbolic predicate outcomes as a generative process, enabling zero-shot composition of learned skills for robotics without retraining.

entry.title: Calibration vs Decision Making: Revisiting the Reliability Paradox in Unlearned Language Models

author.name: Divyaksh Shukla, Ashutosh Modi

entry.summary: Investigates the gap between calibration and decision-making reliability in machine unlearning, showing that low calibration error doesn't imply reliable decision rules as models may use spurious correlations while remaining well-calibrated.

entry.title: Causal Past Logic for Runtime Verification of Distributed LLM Agent Workflows

author.name: Benedikt Bollig

entry.summary: Extends the ZipperGen agent-workflow framework with Causal Past Logic (CPL), a past-time temporal logic for monitoring distributed LLM agent workflows that respects causal visibility in asynchronous execution.

entry.title: DySink: Dynamic Frame Sinks for Autoregressive Long Video Generation

author.name: Bo Ye, Xinyu Cui, Jian Zhao, Tong Wei, Min-Ling Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes DySink for autoregressive long video generation, replacing static early-frame sinks with a retrieval-based framework that maintains a compact memory bank of dynamically relevant frames, avoiding sink collapse.

entry.title: Efficient Learning of Deep State Space Models via Importance Smoothing

author.name: John-Joseph Brady, Nikolas Nusken, Yunpeng Li

entry.summary: Proposes a parallel variational importance smoothing method for training deep state space models that overcomes the sequential bottleneck of SMC-based approaches, enabling better scaling on modern hardware.

entry.title: Stochastic MeanFlow Policies: One-Step Generative Control with Entropic Mirror Descent

author.name: Zeyuan Wang, Da Li, Yulin Chen, Yuehu Gong, Yanming Guo, Ye Shi, Liang Bai, Tianyuan Yu, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: Proposes Stochastic MeanFlow Policies combining one-step generative models with entropic mirror descent for RL, achieving expressiveness of generative policies with tractable entropy estimation.

entry.title: Weasel: Out-of-Domain Generalization for Web Agents via Importance-Diversity Data Selection

author.name: Fatemeh Pesaran zadeh, Seyeon Choi, Xing Han L\`u, Siva Reddy, Gunhee Kim

entry.summary: Proposes Weasel, a trajectory selection method for offline web agent training that optimizes importance-diversity balance over states, websites, and interaction patterns. Improves out-of-domain generalization.

entry.title: Fast Reconstruction of Exact Maxwell Dynamics from Sparse Data

author.name: Dan DeGenaro, Xin Li, Obed Amo, Michael Pokojovy, Sarah Adel Bargal, Markus Lange-Hegermann, Bogdan Rai\c{t}\u{a}

entry.summary: Introduces FLASH-MAX, a shallow neural network architecture for electromagnetic field prediction where each neuron represents an exact Maxwell equation solution. Achieves sub-1% error from ~1K observations in seconds with zero PDE residual.

entry.title: Matryoshka Concept Bottleneck Models

author.name: Ziye Chen, Hongbin Lin, Xinyue Xu, Jie Li, Lijie Hu

entry.summary: Introduces Matryoshka Concept Bottleneck Models that support variable-cost test-time intervention by enabling adaptive concept set sizes without training multiple models, using nested concept representations.

entry.title: Dynamic Shapley Computation

author.name: Xuan Yang, Hsi-Wen Chen, Ming-Syan Chen, Jian Pei

entry.summary: Introduces dynamic Shapley value computation by representing values as a player-by-task matrix and exploiting utility/coalition locality for efficient maintenance as tasks and players evolve.

entry.title: Causal Machine Learning Is Not a Panacea: A Roadmap for Observational Causal Inference in Health

author.name: Donna Tjandra (Division of Computer Science and Engineering, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States), Trenton Chang (Division of Computer Science and Engineering, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States), Sonali Parbhoo (Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Imperial College London, London, UK), Rajesh Ranganath (Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, New York University, New York, New York, United States, Center for Data Science, New York University, New York, New York, United States), Andre Kurepa Waschka (Department of Mathematics & Statistics, Elon University, Elon, North Carolina, United States), William Mitchell (Department of Ophthalmology, Cambridge University Hospitals, Cambridge, UK), Maggie Makar (Division of Computer Science and Engineering, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States), Shalmali Joshi (Department of Biomedical Informatics, Columbia University, New York, New York, United States), Finale Doshi-Velez (School of Engineering and Applied Science, Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States), Leo Anthony Celi (Laboratory for Computational Physiology, Institute for Medical Engineering and Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States, Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, Boston, Massachusetts, United States), Jenna Wiens (Division of Computer Science and Engineering, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States)

entry.summary: Presents a roadmap for applying causal ML to observational health data responsibly, emphasizing validity assumptions, limitations, and the gap between causal ML capabilities and clinical needs.

entry.title: A Typed Tensor Language for Federated Learning

author.name: Theofilos Mailis, Kalliopi-Christina Despotidou, Konstantinos Filippopolitis, Yannis Foufoulas, Thanasis-Michail Karampatsis, Andreas Ktenidis, Evdokia Mailli, Theodore Papamarkou, Yannis Ioannidis

entry.summary: Introduces a typed tensor language that formalizes federated learning as a mathematical structure, proving a shared-state factorization theorem showing typed programs factor through fixed-dimensional shared state independent of client count.

entry.title: Preference-aware Influence-function-based Data Selection Method for Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Qihao Lin, Guanxu Chen, Dongrui Liu, Jing Shao

entry.summary: Proposes PRISM for data selection in LLM fine-tuning that uses the model's current preference to weight target examples via influence functions, prioritizing actionable training data.

entry.title: EvoStruct: Bridging Evolutionary and Structural Priors for Antibody CDR Design via Protein Language Model Adaptation

author.name: Mansoor Ahmed, Sujin Lee, Umar Khayaz, Murray Patterson
